output.methodChoice: C+D: compare IS/IS NOT splits and test rival hypotheses against the eligibility and attrition data.
output.brief: The evidence doesn't support the claim that proximity bias explains the gap. The dashboard divides promotions by all staff, but policy only lets people with 18+ months in their level be nominated. Only 32% of remote staff meet that bar, against 74% of office staff. This is because remote hiring opened widely in July 2024, so most remote staff are new. Among eligible people, the rates are nearly the same: 20.0% remote and 21.1% office. Nomination rates (28.2% vs 28.6%) and approval rates (71% vs 74%) are also close. Remote staff don't leave more often. That rules out attrition. Job-family mix doesn't explain it either, since the gap appears in every family. Caveat: only 110 remote staff are eligible, so a real difference of a few points can't be excluded. Managers' comments hint at some informal favouring of nearby staff for visible work, which is unproven. Don't announce the three-day office rule. It would rest on a misread statistic and would exclude about 180 people hired on home-based contracts. Next: hold the proposal, report promotion rates for eligible staff only, and re-check at the FY2027 cycle. Also track who gets stretch assignments, and tell remote staff how promotion eligibility works.
